notes: SNEWTHook(IPoolManager manager, address launchToken): $poolManager is the chain's Uniswap v4 PoolManager (0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951 on Robinhood Chain) and $token is the SNEWT token the factory deploys just before the hook; the constructor makes no external call. The treasury 0x5f948c351eb9f0734c28b605bbeee9ab9d04318e is a compile-time constant. The hook address must carry exactly the permission bits beforeInitialize (1<<13), beforeSwap (1<<7), afterSwap (1<<6), beforeSwapReturnDelta (1<<3) and afterSwapReturnDelta (1<<2), i.e. address & 0x3FFF == 0x20CC; the constructor reverts with HookAddressNotValid otherwise, so the CREATE2 salt must be mined for that mask. The factory must deploy and initialize atomically with IMD; beforeInitialize does not authenticate the initializer or pin IMD, so separate transactions allow a foreign pair to bind first. beforeInitialize accepts one pool only: the launch token against any paired currency at LP fee 12500 and tick spacing 60, and records the opening time. Fees: the pool keeps its static 1.25% LP fee (never dynamic, never overridden); on top of it the hook takes a fee in the paired currency (IMD) on every swap, 4000 bps at initialization decreasing linearly with block.timestamp to 300 bps over 60 minutes and 300 bps forever after, proportional to the IMD that actually moved through the pool, subject to up to two wei of reservation rounding dust (taken in afterSwap on the unspecified side, or reserved in beforeSwap on the specified side and reconciled in afterSwap). Excess reservation is refunded as an ERC-6909 IMD claim directly to the nonzero recipient encoded as a single canonical 32-byte address in hookData (abi.encode(refundRecipient)); empty, zero or malformed data falls back to the PoolManager caller, usually the router. A delta-only router must forward the explicit recipient to avoid stranding refunds. Full price limits can still partially fill when liquidity is exhausted. Exact-output sells whose fill is below the reservation still require the seller to front IMD and the router to settle IMD in the same transaction, or an authorized claim-burning settlement flow; selecting a refund recipient does not remove that requirement, and TAKE_ALL-only settlement is incompatible with a negative output delta. The fee bound counts the recipient's claim, which they can transfer or redeem separately. Large specified-side requests are limited by uint128 input and int128 full-fill reservation/pool amounts, stricter than an int256-only overflow exception. The fee accrues as the hook's ERC-6909 claim on the PoolManager; sweep(), callable by anyone, delivers all of it to the treasury. Views: feeNow(), openedAt(), pending(), collected(), swept(). No owner, no setters, no proxy, no delegatecall, no selfdestruct.
